report.summary: Reviewed gated_writes.py chunk 4 of 5 (lines 841-1093): _promote_one, promote_candidates, _promote_locked, _governance_verdict, run_write_wave start. Claims checked: several kept, some uncheckable, no broken found.
risks: promote_candidates | medium | not_gated report includes candidates with ok=False but artifact non-empty; if Phase 1 can produce such a candidate, it is silently excluded from 'live' but reported as not_gated, potentially masking a promotable artifact. | Inspect gate_candidates to see whether ok=False can coexist with a non-empty artifact; if impossible, the filter is redundant but harmless.

_promote_one | low | Catch-all catches Exception but not BaseException; KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit would abort the batch, contrary to the 'catch-all' docstring. | Check whether the caller expects to survive KeyboardInterrupt; if yes, broaden to BaseException.

run_write_wave | low | Non-write tasks are dispatched with dry_run=False; if scheduler.dispatch itself can raise, the 'never raises' claim for run_write_wave is not established in this chunk. | Inspect scheduler.dispatch's contract for exceptions.

run_write_wave | low | results list has type list[dict|None]; if other_idx is empty and write_idx non-empty, the final return is not shown in this chunk; if it returns results with None entries, that would violate the position-matched dict contract. | Check the remainder of run_write_wave in the next chunk.

handoff.purpose: Promotion phase: _promote_one, promote_candidates, _promote_locked, _governance_verdict, and start of run_write_wave.

symbols.name: _promote_one
symbols.note: Calls _promote_one_inner; catches Exception and returns a refusal dict with reason 'promotion step raised: ...'.

symbols.name: promote_candidates
symbols.note: Phase 2 entry; filters live candidates, acquires promotion lock, calls _promote_locked, and returns report with promoted/refused/not_gated.

symbols.name: _promote_locked
symbols.note: Creates integration worktree, resolves project test command, loops _promote_one over live candidates, cleans up worktree and branches, returns report with inspect hint.

symbols.name: _governance_verdict
symbols.note: Calls daedalus.core.get_governance; returns (allowed, state, verdict); on import or call failure returns (False, 'unknown', message).

symbols.name: run_write_wave
symbols.note: Wave writer: validates assignment count, separates write vs non-write tasks, dispatches non-write tasks, and (in later chunk) gates write tasks.

symbols.name: AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS
symbols.note: Tuple containing only 'never'; used to coerce legacy auto_promote values.

claims.text: _promote_one_inner already resets the integration worktree to current_head on any failure it anticipates; this is the net under that for the failures it does not.
claims.why: The reset behaviour of _promote_one_inner is in a previous chunk; this chunk only shows the catch-all wrapper.

claims.text: catch-all so ONE candidate's unexpected failure ... reports as a refusal rather than aborting the whole promotion batch.
claims.why: The function wraps _promote_one_inner in try/except Exception and returns a refusal dict for any exception.

claims.text: candidates is what Phase 1 (gate_candidates) returned, in the SAME order they were submitted -- that order is promotion order too
claims.why: The live list is built by iterating candidates in order, and _promote_locked iterates live in that same order.

claims.text: Never raises: every failure mode ... is a refusal in the returned report, not an exception.
claims.why: The function catches PromotionUnavailable from the lock, but _promote_locked and GitWorktreeManager methods could raise; their exception handling is not fully shown in this chunk.

claims.text: cancel is forwarded to every STALENESS-triggered regeneration (_reattempt's own TaskAttempt ...) AND to the cumulative re-gate's own command_gate call inside _promote_one_inner
claims.why: This chunk shows cancel being passed to _promote_locked, but the forwarding to _reattempt and command_gate happens in _promote_one_inner, which is in a previous chunk.

claims.text: A cancellation landing there is reported distinctly (_CumulativeGateCancelled in the refusal reason, never conflated with an ordinary cumulative gate failed)
claims.why: The distinct reporting logic is in _promote_one_inner, not in this chunk.

claims.text: the SAME unconditional git reset --hard/clean -fd that already runs for a genuine cumulative-gate failure also runs for a cancelled one
claims.why: The reset/clean logic is in _promote_one_inner, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Reported, not dropped: a candidate that never reached STATE_CLEAN in Phase 1 ... has nothing to promote, but silently omitting it here would make this report LOOK complete ... Filtered by object IDENTITY
claims.why: not_gated is built from candidates whose id is not in live_ids, and live_ids is a set of id(c) for live candidates.

claims.text: two distinct candidates can legitimately compare equal on fields.
claims.why: Filtering by id(c) rather than dataclass equality confirms identity-based filtering.

claims.text: if ledger_error or ledger_path is None: ... refused with 'ledger unavailable'
claims.why: The code returns refused entries for each live candidate when ledger_path is None or ledger_error is truthy.

claims.text: lock unavailable ... is a refusal in the returned report, not an exception.
claims.why: PromotionUnavailable is caught and converted to a report with refused entries.

claims.text: integration worktree has no readable gitdir pointer; refusing to promote into it unpinned
claims.why: If git.admin_dir is None, the function returns refused for all live candidates with that reason.

claims.text: no file in the primary checkout was changed; nothing is merged until a human (or a separately-invoked step) acts on the integration branch above
claims.why: The function only works in the integration worktree and returns an inspect hint; it does not touch the primary checkout.

claims.text: AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS = ('never',) ... The only production-capable value is 'never'; legacy values cannot reach promote_candidates.
claims.why: The comment claims legacy values cannot reach promote_candidates, but that enforcement is in a previous chunk or elsewhere; this chunk only defines the tuple and coerces in run_write_wave.

claims.text: _governance_verdict ... read straight off daedalus.core.get_governance, never re-derived here.
claims.why: The function imports and calls get_governance directly.

claims.text: Any failure to even ASK the question ... reports the vocabulary's unknown, not a silent True.
claims.why: Both import failure and call failure return (False, 'unknown', message).

claims.text: unknown and absent stay distinct facts ... this only ever manufactures unknown for a failure that happened HERE; a real absent receipt is already reported correctly by get_governance itself and passes through unchanged.
claims.why: The function uses gov.get('state') or 'unknown' only when gov exists; it does not coerce an absent state to unknown unless get_governance returns an empty dict or missing state.

claims.text: cancel, when given, is forwarded to gate_candidates for every concurrent attempt in this wave.
claims.why: The forwarding to gate_candidates is not in this chunk; it occurs later in the function.

claims.text: None (the default) is byte-identical to this function's behaviour before cancel existed: no caller that does not pass it is affected.
claims.why: The behaviour with cancel=None is not fully visible until the rest of the function is seen.

claims.text: assignments MUST be scheduler.accept(tasks, repo_root=repo_root)'s own return, in the SAME order as tasks ... Passed in once, length-checked, used once.
claims.why: The function checks len(assignments) == len(tasks) and uses assignments only to compute write_idx and other_idx.

claims.text: Recomputing it here would still be SAFE (accept is a pure classification ... two calls on the same tasks always agree)
claims.why: The purity of accept is not verifiable in this chunk; it is a claim about another function.

claims.text: Returns one result dict per entry in tasks, position-matched
claims.why: The final return is at the end of the function, not in this chunk; the results list is initialized to None and filled for other_idx, but write results are not yet assigned.

claims.text: Non-write tasks in the SAME wave ... are NOT touched by the gated path: they are delegated back to scheduler.dispatch, scoped to just their own indices
claims.why: other_idx is computed and other_tasks are dispatched via scheduler.dispatch for those indices only.

claims.text: NEVER writes the primary checkout and never calls promote_candidates.
claims.why: This chunk shows no primary checkout writes or promote_candidates call, but the rest of the function is not yet seen.

claims.text: Legacy auto_promote values are reported as denied input and coerced to 'never'.
claims.why: The coercion to 'never' is visible, but the reporting of denied input is not yet visible in this chunk.

observations.what: The catch-all in _promote_one catches Exception but not BaseException; KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit would still abort the batch.
The not_gated list includes candidates that are not in live_ids but may have ok=False and a non-empty artifact; if Phase 1 can produce such a candidate, it would be silently excluded from promotion.
promote_candidates calls _promote_locked without a try/except; if _promote_locked raises (e.g., GitWorktreeManager.create_worktree fails), the 'Never raises' claim would be broken.
run_write_wave dispatches non-write tasks with dry_run=False and no exception handling; if dispatch raises, the wave aborts.
The results list is typed list[dict|None]; if the final return occurs with None entries (e.g., write_idx non-empty but write results not filled), the position-matched contract would be violated.
